title: POC data processing addendum — workshop draft
body:
Context and purpose:
This document captures the output from the Solutions Engineering workshop on POC-level data handling expectations (customer: Acme Retail, workshop 2025-11-01). It is a working draft of a short-form Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and retention proposals intended to be attached to POC statements of work. The goal: provide a clear, minimal set of commitments and configuration options for customers evaluating Redwood in hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes.

Scope:
- Applies only to POCs and proofs-of-value where the Customer has not yet executed an enterprise DPA; designed to be short-lived and configurable.
- Covers categories of data Redwood will process during the POC (inputs, outputs, logs, telemetry, KV/prefix caches, embeddings, backups).
- Proposes retention periods, deletion procedures, subprocessors, international transfer approach, and breach notification timelines.

High-level design principles used in the workshop:
1) Minimum necessary: default behavior is to retain the bare minimum required to operate the POC and troubleshoot issues.
2) Mode-sensitive defaults: hosted vs. dedicated vs. private have different default retention and access assumptions.
3) Customer overrides: customers can request stricter retention or retention extension for debugging with explicit scope and expiry.
4) Transparent subprocessors and transfers: list the likely subprocessors and the cross-border approach clearly.

Data categories (POC examples):
- Customer prompts and system inputs (text/files sent to the API).
- Model outputs (generated text, structured outputs, tool call parameters).
- Embeddings vectors created during the POC.
- KV/prefix cache entries (runtime cache to speed inference).
- Request/response metadata (timestamps, model id, latency, route).
- Operational logs and traces (application logs, stack traces on error).
- Billing/usage records (token counts, route usage).
- Backups and snapshots of dedicated/private infra (disk snapshots, database backups).

Proposed retention defaults by deployment mode (workshop proposal):
1) Hosted (Redwood-managed clusters):
   - Request/response payloads (inputs + outputs): 7 days default; purge on customer request or at POC termination.
   - Embeddings: 30 days default; can be reduced to 7 days or configured to never persist beyond request if customer requires.
   - KV/prefix caches: ephemeral (no persisted disk writes) by default; if persistence enabled for performance, retained 14 days.
   - Operational logs/traces: 30 days for debugging, 90 days aggregated metrics only; full traces only with customer consent.
   - Billing/usage: 1 year (for billing reconciliation).

2) Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity):
   - Request/response payloads: retained per customer config; default 30 days but option to set 0 (no retention) for stricter customers.
   - Embeddings: default 90 days; recommended customer-managed storage for long-lived embedding catalogs.
   - KV/prefix caches: may be persisted for performance; retention controlled by customer policy (we recommend TTL 14 days for POC workloads).
   - Operational logs: 90 days unless customer requires shorter retention; aggregated metrics kept 1 year.

3) Private (VPC or on-prem):
   - Redwood control plane retains only minimal bookkeeping (POC metadata, invoice record).
   - All PII and payloads to be stored in customer infrastructure by default; Redwood-service-run components only access ephemeral in-memory caches unless explicitly allowed in SOW.
   - Backups: handled by customer; Redwood may provide backup scripts and guidance.

Encryption and access controls:
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ for API traffic.
- Data at rest: AES-256 encryption for persisted payloads and backups in Redwood-managed storage.
- Key management: Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default; customers can request use of customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private within the SOW.
- Role-based access: production-side logs and PII access is restricted to named Redwood engineers on a need-to-know basis; access requires approval and is logged.
- Audit trail: redaction and access logs retained according to the retention table above.

Subprocessors and transfers:
- Likely subprocessors: cloud hosting providers (AWS/GCP), monitoring providers (PagerDuty, Datadog), analytics (Mixpanel), CI/CD (GitHub Actions). Exact list to be provided in final addendum.
- Cross-border: Hosted customers default to region-based routing; data may be transferred across regions for disaster recovery. For customers requiring strict residency, recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.

Deletion and purge procedures:
- Ad hoc deletion: Customer may request deletion of any stored payloads; Redwood will confirm deletion completion within 72 hours and provide a deletion report.
- Systematic purge: automated purge jobs run daily to remove data older than retention windows.
- Snapshots/backups: deletion of backups may take longer (up to 7 days) due to backup lifecycle; where necessary, snapshots will be manually removed with attestation.

Breach notification and incident handling:
- Notification timeline: Redwood commits to notify Customer within 72 hours of discovery of a confirmed breach affecting PII or payload data.
- Incident support: Redwood will provide log excerpts, mitigation steps, and recommended remediation; details and scope of support depend on SOW and support tier.

Sample contract language (short-form DPA clause suggestions) — use in POC SOW:
"Data Processing Addendum (POC):
1) Purpose: Redwood Inference will process Customer Data solely to provide POC services as described in the SOW.
2) Categories of data: inputs, outputs, telemetry, and operational logs as defined in Appendix A.
3) Retention: data will be retained according to the configuration selected by the Customer and the defaults in Appendix B; Customer may request immediate deletion.
4) Subprocessors: Redwood will maintain a list of subprocessors and provide notification of changes.
5) International transfer: Redwood may transfer data between regions for operational reasons unless Customer selects region-locking (available for Dedicated/Private).
6) Security: Redwood implements industry-standard controls (TLS, AES-256 at rest, RBAC).
7) Breach notification: Redwood will notify within 72 hours and provide reasonable assistance for remediation.
8) Termination: on POC termination Redwood will delete Customer Data in accordance with the selected retention setting and provide a deletion certificate on request."

Appendix A (short): examples and preservation notes:
- Example: A customer support POC where transcripts are sent to Redwood. If Customer selects "no retention", Redwood will not persist transcripts beyond in-memory processing. For hosted POCs with debugging enabled, transcripts may be retained up to 7 days.

Appendix B (default retention table):
- Inputs/Outputs: Hosted 7d, Dedicated 30d default, Private customer-managed.
- Embeddings: Hosted 30d, Dedicated 90d, Private customer-managed.
- Operational logs (debug traces): Hosted 30d, Dedicated 90d, Private per customer infra.
- Billing records: all modes 1y.

Workshop notes and open items (actionable):
1) Customer asked for an option: "ephemeral mode" where no payloads or embeddings are ever written to disk. Action: engineering to document and provide a config flag and test matrix. Owner: Ethan Morales. Due: 2025-11-10.
2) Need an attestation template for deletion of backups/snapshots for hosted POCs. Owner: Sofia Lin + Legal. Due: 2025-11-14.
3) Draft a short checkbox UI for the POC onboarding flow which lets customers select retention presets (ephemeral / debug-7d / debug-30d / custom). Owner: Marcus Rivera (Console). Due: 2025-11-21.
4) Clarify whether embeddings used for vector search in POC are considered "Customer Data" if not retained beyond runtime. Action: Product to confirm. Owner: Priya Kapoor. Due: 2025-11-07.
5) Provide final subprocessor list and an easy way for customers to opt-out of certain analytics subprocessors during POC. Owner: Compliance team. Due: 2025-11-17.

Unresolved questions surfaced in the workshop (for legal/product):
- What level of deletion attestation is sufficient for enterprise customers evaluating Redwood as a SOC2/ISO buyer?
- Are we comfortable with 72-hour deletion confirmation SLA for all hosted POCs, or should critical POCs have a faster SLA?
- For Dedicated POCs where we need to keep logs for debugging, can we provide per-record redaction so PII is stripped before retention?

Communication plan with customer:
- Send this draft as "Workshop follow-up: POC Data Handling + DPA draft" with callouts for configurable choices.
- Offer a 30-minute follow-up to walk through retention presets and onboarding checklist.
- Provide a copy of the deletion attestation and subprocessor list with the final SOW.

Quick onboarding checklist for SEs running POCs:
- Confirm deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and region.
- Select retention preset in onboarding.
- Confirm KMS choice (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed).
- Confirm whether embeddings should persist beyond the session.
- Add deletion attestation request to SOW if customer requires.

Appendix C: Communications snippets for proposals (one-liners SEs can paste) :
- "We default to ephemeral handling for POC payloads; you can opt into short-term retention for debugging and extend only with explicit consent."
- "For strict residency we recommend Dedicated capacity or Private deployment; hosted POCs may cross regions for resilience."

Notes-to-self / SE shorthand (raw):
- Don’t forget: hosted debug logs = opt-in. Default is minimal.
- Keep the DPA short; legal will expand for enterprise. This is a POC-level commitment only.

Next steps (this doc):
- Incorporate feedback from Legal and Compliance into the final POC DPA template. (Legal reviewer: Ana Mendes).
- Add ephemeral-mode config and console checkbox to POC onboarding flows and test in staging.
- Send follow-up to Acme Retail and schedule a 30-min call to lock retention settings.

Contact and owners (workshop):
- SE lead: Priya Kapoor (pri@redwood.ai)
- Eng lead (retention work): Ethan Morales
- Console UX: Marcus Rivera
- Legal reviewer: Ana Mendes

Revision history (work-in-progress):
- 2025-11-03 initial workshop notes and first draft retention table (Priya)
- 2025-11-07 updated with engineering feasibility notes (Ethan)
- 2025-11-12 added attestation and action owners (Sofia)

End of draft — this is intentionally iterative. Mark anything you disagree with as an inline comment or Slack DM the SE channel.
